observation.visible_scene: A close-up, static view of a decorated Christmas tree. Two small lantern-shaped ornaments hang from a thin wire/string across the middle of the frame (one near center-right, one at left), surrounded by red tinsel, dark green pine needles, and out-of-focus colored bokeh lights (green, blue, red, yellow) in the background. The physical layout of the branches, tinsel, hanging wire, and ornaments does not change position during the excerpt.
visible_changes: The illuminated panels inside the hanging lantern ornaments cycle between two color states: a warm orange/amber glow and a cool bright white-blue glow. The center-right lantern shows orange in early frames (1-4), switches to white-blue (5-11), back to orange (12-17), white-blue again (18-24), orange (25-30), white-blue (31-37), and orange (38-41).
The left lantern shifts in a similar alternating manner, appearing warm orange in some frames and pale green/white in others, roughly tracking the center lantern's on/off color cycle.
The surrounding bokeh background lights show minor brightness/color shimmer but no positional movement.
No camera pan, tilt, or zoom is evident; the framing of the tree and ornaments remains fixed throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: The complete color sequence and its period (the excerpt begins and ends mid-cycle, so the full pattern of orange/white transitions before t=0 and after t=2.669 is unknown).
Whether other ornaments or background lights change color on their own schedule or in sync with the lanterns.
What controls or triggers the color change (no operator or mechanism is visible).
uncertain_details: The exact hue boundaries between 'white' and 'blue' and between 'orange' and 'amber' inside the lanterns vary frame to frame, likely due to exposure and surrounding reflections rather than a third distinct color state.
Any very small camera or branch micro-motion is below reliable detection; the scene is treated as effectively static.
